11.PROGESTOGEN-ONLY PILL
•This guideline will consider POPs available in the UK. namely Desogestrel (DSG) 75 kg, Drosperinone (DRSP) 4 mg (soon to be available in the UK) and the ‘traditional’ POPs levonorgestrel| (LNG) 30 pg and norethisterone (NET) 350 ug
•MOA: DSG and DRSP POPs: inhibition of ovulation
•LNG and NET POPs: changes on cervical mucus, endometrium and tubal motility
•A 12-month supply of traditional, DSG or DRSP POP can be provided with an annual review.
•Specific approved brands of DSG POP can now be bought from a pharmacy, without a prescription, under the supervision of a pharmacist.
•LNG, NET and DSG POPs are taken continuously at 24-hour intervals without an HFI.
•The new DRSP POP is taken in a regimen of 24 daily active pills followed by four hormone-free placebo pills (to establish a more predictable bleeding pattern)
•Use of all POPs taken between menarche and age 55 years.

 

⇨DRSP POP should also generally be avoided in:
1.Severe renal insufficiency or acute renal failure.
2.Individuals with known hyperkaliemia or untreated hyperaldosteronism (e.g., Addison's disease).
3.Individuals currently using potassium-sparing diuretics, aldosterone antagonists or potassium supplements.

DRSP POP used with caution by individuals with mild/moderate renal impairment or treated hyperaldosteronism (e.g., treated Addison's disease)

•Individuals with significant risk factors for chronic kidney disease: measurement of urea & electrolytes (U&E) and blood pressure considered prior to prescription of the DRSP POP, particularly if age over 50 years
⇨Side effects: Change in bleeding pattern over a 3-month period ending at about 12 months of use (at around 6—9 months of use with DRSP POP)
⇨Interactions: contraceptive effectiveness of all POPs could be reduced during use of the enzyme-inducer and for 28 days after stopping the enzyme-inducer.
•Ability of UPA-EC as an EC can be reduced if a POP has been taken in the preceding 7 days or within 5 days of taking the UPA. Offer them DMPA. the Cu-lUD or the LNG-IUS
•Interactions between DRSP POP and drugs such as ACEi and ARBs could also potentially increase risk of hyperkaliemia
⇨Non-contraceptive benefits:
oDSG and DRSP POP could reduce dysmenorrhea for some users
oDRSP POP might theoretically offer benefit for acne or hirsutism

Induction of withdrawal bleeding is not required in individuals with PCOS during use of a POP even if they are amenorrhea.

 

 

AC: additional contraception like barrier or abstinence

•DRSP POP is started on day 1 of a natural menstrual cycle, day 1 after abortion or by day 21 after childbirth. If started at any other time, quick start+ AC for 7 days+ consider EC and follow-up pregnancy test
•LNG, NET and DSG POPs can be started on days 1—5 of a natural menstrual cycle, by day 5 after abortion or by day 21 after childbirth. At any other time. quick start +AC for 2 days+ consider EC and follow-up pregnancy test if required.
•(UPSI from the time that the first pill was missed until correct pill taking had resumed for 48 hours)
•DRSP POP if taken 24hrs late recent pill + next pill at usual time+ AC for 7days+ consider EC

•POPs are taken daily with no pill-free interval.
•taken at or around the same POPs currently available in the UK contain either NET 350 pg (Micronor, Noriday), LNG 30 pg (Norgeston@) or DSG 75 pg (Cerazetto)
⇨Mode of action:
•POPs increase volume & viscosity of cervical mucus preventing sperm penetration into upper reproductive tract. Can also act to suppress ovulation.
⇨Efficacy:
•If used consistently and correctly, POPs are more than 99% effective.
⇨Drug interactions:
•POP users taking enzyme-inducing drugs should be advised to switch to the progestogen-only injectable or intrauterine contraception.
•For short durations of enzyme-inducing treatment (<2 months) women can continue the POP providing they use additional precautions
•Women wishing to start the POP after stopping enzyme-inducing drugs should be advised dafter the last dose of enzyme-inducing drug.
⇨Missed Pill Guideline:

TRADITIONAL POPS DESOGESTREL POPS

> 3 hours late >12 hours late

 

(>27 hours since the last pill was taken) (>36 hours since the last pill was taken)

•The missed pill should be taken as soon as remembered. If more than one pill has been missed, only one pill should be taken.
•The next pill should be taken at the usual time. This may mean that two pills are taken in 1 day.
•Additional contraceptive precautions (condoms or avoidance of sex) are advised for 2 days (48 hours) after restarting the POP.
•Emergency contraception is indicated if unprotected sexual intercourse occurred after the missed pill and within 48 hours of restarting the POP.
⇨Raised BMI and POP:
✓NO increased risk of pregnancy in POP users with a heavier body weight or a higher BMI and insufficient evidence to support a dose of more than one pill per day in women who are heavy or overweight.
❖Non-contraceptive benefits:
✓Dysmenorrhea: DSG
✓Ectopic pregnancy: While the overall risk of pregnancy is reduced with use of traditional POPs, around 1 in 10 pregnancies that do occur may be ectopic.
✓Headaches and Ovarian cysts/persistent ovarian follicles: No good evidence was identified.
✓Return of fertility: There is no evidence suggesting a delay in return of fertility following discontinuation of a POP; therefore, if pregnancy is not desired, other contraceptive methods should be used immediately following discontinuation of the POP.
❖Side effects:
✓Bleeding: Changes in bleeding patterns associated with the POP are common.
✓Libido: Effects of POP on libido are lacking and therefore a possible effect cannot be excluded.
✓Weight change: Evidence does not support a casual association between POP use and weight change.
▪Women may be given up to a 12-month supply of POPs at their first and follow-up visits and advised to return at any time if problems arise.
▪The POP can be used until the age of 55 years when natural loss of fertility can be assumed for most women.

If they are aged > 50 years and amenorrhea they can continue using a POP and have FSH concentrations tested on two occasions 6 weeks apart. If both FSH measurements are >30 IU/I this is

▪suggestive of ovarian failure and they should continue with a POP or barrier method for one further year.'

When is a pill missed?

A pill is missed if taken 3 hours late (27 hours after last pill taken)

A pill is missed if taken 12 hours last (36 hours after les pill

A pill is missed if taken 24 hours late 48 hours after last pill was taken or 24 hours after a new packet should have been started after an HFI

Action if pill(s) missed

  • •Take the most recent missed pill as soon as possible
  • •Take the next pill at the usual time (this may mean taking two pills in 1 day)
  • •Use additional contraceptive precautions (eg, condoms) for 48 hours after correct pill-taking has restarted
  • •Consider EC

  • •Take the next bill at the usual time (this may mean taking two pills in 1 day)
  • •Use additional contraceptive precautions (eg, condoms) for 7 days after correct pill-taking has restarted
  • •Consider EC
  • •OMIT THE HFI (PLACEBO PILLS) IF ANY OF THE LAST 7 ACTIVE PILLS ARE MISSED

Is EC required?

EC should be considered if there was UPSI from the site that the first pill was missed until correct pill taking had resumed for 48 hours

  • •EC should be considered if
  • •Any active pill(s) were missed and there was UPSI from the time that the first pill was missed until correct pill-taking had resumed for 7 days
  • •Pills were missed on days 1-7 of the packet and there was UPSI during the HFI or week 1

Follow-up

Consider pregnancy test 21 days after last UPSI
